CWE-319.name: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
CWE-319.description: The product transmits sensitive or security-critical data in cleartext across physical or network communication channels, allowing any unauthorized actor with channel access to sniff, intercept, or modify the data.
threat_scenarios: Eavesdropping and packet sniffing on local Wi-Fi or upstream networks via Wireshark or tcpdump.
Cleartext extraction of administrative credentials and Wi-Fi WPA2 pre-shared keys.
Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) session injection and unauthorized router reconfiguration.
CWE-319.mitigation: Enforce cryptographic transport protocols (TLS 1.2/1.3, SSHv2) for all administrative and management data. Disable unencrypted Telnet and HTTP services.

CWE-345.name: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
threat_scenarios: DNS Cache Poisoning and DNS Spoofing attacks targeting weak Transaction ID (TXID) entropy in embedded forwarders.
DNSpooq vulnerability exploitation redirecting victim traffic to malicious phishing portals.
Acceptance of forged upstream router advertisements or configuration payloads.
CWE-345.mitigation: Enable DNSSEC validation, implement cryptographically random query source ports and transaction IDs, and verify message integrity signatures before accepting data.

CWE-400.name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption (Amplification Abuse)
CWE-400.description: The product does not properly control the allocation or consumption of a limited resource (such as CPU, bandwidth, or network socket handles), enabling attackers to exhaust system capacity or leverage the device for DDoS amplification.
threat_scenarios: Open DNS resolver abuse where spoofed UDP queries trigger high-bandwidth responses directed at external victim targets.
Resource exhaustion on lightweight embedded MIPS/ARM CPUs causing device lockup or denial of service.
Connection table saturation disabling legitimate client connectivity.
affected_components: DNS Forwarder Listening on External Interfaces (0.0.0.0:53)
CWE-400.mitigation: Bind DNS services strictly to internal LAN interfaces (bind-interfaces), implement query rate-limiting, and drop inbound WAN requests using iptables firewall rules.

CWE-798.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
threat_scenarios: Automated Mirai-style dictionary botnet attacks harvesting factory-default credentials.
Extraction of static credentials from client HTML source code or strings in firmware images.
Global administrative takeover across all deployed units sharing the identical firmware build.
CWE-798.mitigation: Never embed static default passwords in firmware. Force the user to create a unique password upon first boot, or generate unique randomized factory keys per physical unit.

CWE-259.name: Use of Hardcoded Password
CWE-259.description: The product uses a hardcoded password for inbound authentication or communication with external services, rendering security dependent on secrecy of static data.
threat_scenarios: Telnet/SSH automated brute-forcing using vendor default password lists.
Firmware reverse engineering revealing undocumented diagnostic passwords.
CWE-259.mitigation: Disable default shared passwords. Implement cryptographically generated unique credentials per device label.

CWE-352.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
CWE-352.description: The web application does not verify whether a received HTTP request was intentionally submitted by the authenticated user, allowing malicious external websites to forge administrative state changes.
threat_scenarios: A logged-in administrator visits a malicious web page which silently sends an HTTP POST/GET request changing the repeater's DNS servers or Wi-Fi password.
Remote execution of configuration commands without the user's knowledge.
CWE-352.mitigation: Implement unique cryptographic anti-CSRF tokens for all state-changing operations and configure SameSite=Strict cookies.

CWE-306.name: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
CWE-306.description: The product does not perform any authentication for functionality that requires a provable user identity or administrative authority.
threat_scenarios: Any unauthenticated user on the local Wi-Fi clicks login and gains direct access to router settings without password prompt.
Direct invocation of administrative CGI URLs without prior authentication.
CWE-306.mitigation: Enforce strict session and credential authentication on all administrative endpoints and dashboard pages.

CWE-312.name: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
CWE-312.description: The product stores sensitive information in cleartext without applying appropriate encryption or reversible encoding safeguards.
threat_scenarios: Storing Base64-encoded administrative passwords in client browser cookies.
Cleartext password storage in NVRAM or unencrypted configuration backup files.
CWE-312.mitigation: Store opaque, cryptographically random session tokens instead of user credentials in browser cookies. Use salted hash algorithms (Argon2 / PBKDF2) for stored passwords.

CWE-1004.name: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag
CWE-1004.description: The product sets a sensitive cookie without the HttpOnly attribute, allowing client-side scripts to access the cookie content.
threat_scenarios: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) payload reads the session cookie and transmits it to an attacker-controlled server.
CWE-1004.mitigation: Always append '; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict' to all authentication and session Set-Cookie HTTP headers.

CWE-598.name: Use of GET Request Method with Sensitive Query Strings
CWE-598.description: The web application transmits sensitive parameters (such as passwords or session tokens) within the query string of an HTTP GET request.
threat_scenarios: Passphrases logged in plaintext across browser history, web proxy logs, and server access logs.
Credentials leaked via HTTP Referer headers when navigating to external links.
affected_components: Login Form Action (GET instead of POST)
CWE-598.mitigation: Submit authentication credentials strictly via HTTP POST request bodies over HTTPS TLS connections.

CWE-613.name: Insufficient Session Expiration
CWE-613.description: The product does not sufficiently expire active sessions after a period of inactivity or provide a mechanism for explicit session termination.
threat_scenarios: Shared or public workstation retains administrative access indefinitely after configuration.
Session fixation and persistent replay of unexpired administrative tokens.
CWE-613.mitigation: Provide a prominent 'Logout' button that destroys server-side session state and invalidate sessions after a configurable inactivity timeout.

CWE-1277.name: Firmware Not Updateable
CWE-1277.description: The hardware product or firmware does not provide a secure, reliable mechanism to update its firmware or receive vendor security patches.
threat_scenarios: Permanent exposure to known vulnerabilities (e.g. DNSpooq, Mirai exploits) with zero patching capability.
Abandoned white-label IoT devices leaving consumer networks perpetually compromised.
CWE-1277.mitigation: Establish an official vendor support repository, provide cryptographically verified OTA update mechanisms, and publish vulnerability advisories.

CWE-1059.name: Incomplete Documentation and Support
CWE-1059.description: The vendor does not provide adequate documentation, security contact details, or support infrastructure for the software or hardware product.
threat_scenarios: Inability for consumers to identify genuine firmware builds or report newly discovered security flaws to the manufacturer.
CWE-1059.mitigation: Publish transparent vendor security policies, CVE tracking, and verified firmware download portals.

CWE-321.name: Use of Hardcoded Cryptographic Key
CWE-321.description: The product uses a hardcoded cryptographic key, which is shared across all instances of the product or embedded in binary images.
threat_scenarios: Attackers extract private TLS or SSH keys from firmware images to decrypt network traffic or impersonate devices in MitM attacks.
CWE-321.mitigation: Generate unique cryptographic keys and certificates during first boot or per-device factory provisioning. Never embed shared private keys in firmware binaries.

CWE-347.name: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
CWE-347.description: The product does not verify or incorrectly verifies the cryptographic signature of data, files, or firmware updates before execution or flashing.
threat_scenarios: Flashing unauthorized, malicious firmware images containing backdoors, keyloggers, or persistent rootkits.
Tampering with update binaries during transit over unencrypted connections.
CWE-347.mitigation: Enforce asymmetric digital signature verification (e.g. RSA-PSS or Ed25519) on all firmware packages before writing to flash memory.

CWE-287.name: Improper Authentication
threat_scenarios: Observed technical exposure matching MITRE CWE-287 standards.
Potential vulnerability exploitation in IoT and embedded network routers.
CWE-287.mitigation: Follow standard MITRE remediation guidelines and vendor security best practices.

CWE-200.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
threat_scenarios: Observed technical exposure matching MITRE CWE-200 standards.
Potential vulnerability exploitation in IoT and embedded network routers.
CWE-200.mitigation: Follow standard MITRE remediation guidelines and vendor security best practices.

CWE-494.name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
threat_scenarios: Observed technical exposure matching MITRE CWE-494 standards.
Potential vulnerability exploitation in IoT and embedded network routers.
CWE-494.mitigation: Follow standard MITRE remediation guidelines and vendor security best practices.
